hook: Kids mailed real candy to a cartoon boy.
fact: It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown debuted on CBS in 1966, and in it Charlie Brown gets a rock at every house while trick or treating. Young viewers felt so bad for him that they mailed piles of candy to CBS.
backbone: A whole country tried to fix a single bad Halloween.
source: TheWrap, "It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown" at 50: https://www.thewrap.com/great-pumpkin-charlie-brown-50th-daughter-schulz-peanuts-creator-halloween-rocks/
quote: When the half-hour television special debuted in 1966, the sequence had young fans feeling so bad for Charlie, they mailed piles of candy to CBS.
visual: a small paper trick or treat bag holding 3 smooth gray rocks on a wooden porch step, warm porch light

hook: The scariest mask of 1978 started as Captain Kirk.
fact: The mask worn by Michael Myers in Halloween (1978) began as a William Shatner Captain Kirk mask. Production designer Tommy Lee Wallace painted it white, pulled off the sideburns, and cut the eyeholes wider.
backbone: A hero's face, emptied out, became the fear.
quote: I had, meanwhile, modified the Kirk mask a little - painted it dead white, yanked off the sideburns, opened up the eyeholes more, mussed the hair and darkened it.
visual: a blank white rubber mask on a plain wooden table beside a can of white spray paint, single lamp

hook: Halloween's autumn town was filmed in a Los Angeles spring.
fact: The fictional town of Haddonfield in Halloween (1978) was built entirely from Los Angeles locations in the spring of 1978. With a budget of about $300,000, the production could not afford to leave Los Angeles to find a storybook autumn.
backbone: The fall you remember was made in sunshine.
source: Los Angeles Magazine, Every Famous Filming Location from John Carpenter's Halloween: https://lamag.com/film/halloween-locations-40/
quote: The small, fictional town of Haddonfield, which was named after the historic New Jersey town where Debra Hill grew up, was created completely with practical L.A. locations during the spring of 1978.
visual: a handful of dry brown leaves scattered on a sunny sidewalk under a green palm shadow

hook: Thriller was the first music video the Library of Congress kept.
fact: In 2009, Michael Jackson's Thriller became the first music video named to the National Film Registry of the Library of Congress. The 1983 video, directed by John Landis, was 1 of 25 films chosen that year for preservation.
backbone: The graveyard dance is now officially history.
source: CBS News, "Thriller," Muppets in U.S. Film Registry: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/thriller-muppets-in-us-film-registry/
quote: It's the first music video named to the registry.
visual: a red zip jacket folded on a record crate next to a stack of cassette tapes, dim amber light

hook: Monster Mash hit No. 1 here and got banned in Britain.
fact: Monster Mash reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 on October 20, 1962, just before Halloween. BBC Radio banned it as too morbid, and the song came back onto the charts in 1970 and again in 1973.
backbone: A silly song kept finding its way home.
source: HISTORY, "Monster Mash" hits No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart: https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/october-20/monster-mash-hits-number-one
quote: BBC Radio banned it, saying it was 'too morbid' to play on the air.
visual: a 45 rpm record on a turntable with a small carved pumpkin beside it, warm lamp glow

hook: The book you traded at recess topped a banned list.
fact: The Scary Stories series by Alvin Schwartz ranked No. 1 on the American Library Association's list of the 100 most frequently challenged books of 1990 to 1999. It placed above every other title on that list for the decade.
backbone: What scared the adults most was the book itself.
source: American Library Association, Top 100 Most Frequently Challenged Books: 1990-1999: https://www.ala.org/advocacy/bbooks/100-most-frequently-challenged-books-1990%E2%80%931999
visual: a worn paperback face down on a sleeping bag beside a lit flashlight, dark room

hook: A movie that opens in a library is now shelved there.
fact: Ghostbusters (1984) was added to the Library of Congress National Film Registry in December 2015. Director Ivan Reitman noted that the film begins with a ghost in a library.
backbone: The story came full circle, right back to the stacks.
source: CBS News, "Shawshank Redemption," "Ghostbusters" added to National Film Registry: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/shawshank-redemption-ghostbusters-added-to-national-film-registry-2/
quote: It's an honor to know that a movie that begins with a ghost in a library, now has a spot on the shelves of the Library of Congress.
visual: a quiet library aisle with a card catalog drawer pulled open and soft green lamp light

hook: In 1999, theaters handed out missing person flyers.
fact: At screenings of The Blair Witch Project, the filmmakers handed out missing person flyers for the 3 students in the film and asked audiences for information. The film's website added fake historical documents and news interviews, and those materials are now held by the University of Pittsburgh Library System.
backbone: The scare began before the lights went down.
source: University of Pittsburgh, Pittwire, The Blair Witch Project archive has joined Pitt's Horror Studies Collection: https://www.pittwire.pitt.edu/features-articles/2025/02/25/blair-witch-project-horror-studies-archive
quote: During 'The Blair Witch Project' screenings, the filmmakers would go as far as to distribute missing person flyers of the three students, which are included in the ULS collection, asking audience members to come forward if they knew any information about the students.
visual: a photocopied paper flyer pinned to a bare tree trunk in a gray autumn forest

hook: The first Treehouse of Horror ended with Edgar Allan Poe.
fact: The Simpsons aired its first Treehouse of Horror on October 25, 1990. Its final segment was an earnest retelling of Poe's The Raven, narrated by James Earl Jones, with Bart animated as the bird.
backbone: A cartoon handed a generation its first Poe.
source: Ultimate Classic Rock, 'The Simpsons' Airs its First 'Treehouse of Horror': https://ultimateclassicrock.com/simpsons-treehouse-of-horror-anniversary/
quote: The third and final vignette of the first "Treehouse of Horror" was "The Raven," an earnest retelling of the famous Edgar Allan Poe poem.
visual: a black feather resting on an open old poetry book beside a tube television, lamp light

hook: The Owens house in Practical Magic was mostly hollow.
fact: The Owens family house in Practical Magic (1998) was built on bare land in San Juan County Park in Washington state, and it was largely a hollow shell. The studio promised to take it down, and it was dismantled the day after filming wrapped.
backbone: The house we all wanted only stood for a season.
source: HistoryLink.org, Filming of movie Practical Magic begins on Whidbey Island on April 6, 1998: https://www.historylink.org/File/11238
quote: The reality is that the house, constructed on a bare piece of land in San Juan County Park, about six miles due west across San Juan Island from Friday Harbor, was largely a hollow shell.
visual: a white Victorian porch railing with a jar of dried herbs and lavender, gray sea light
